1.1: This Paul talkin', called to be one of Jesus Christ's apostles, not by my own doing, but by God's will. Sosthenes, our brother, right here with me.
1.2: To God's church out in Corinth—to all y'all who've been set apart in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, along with everybody everywhere callin' on Jesus' name. He our Lord—yours and mine.
1.3: Grace and peace to y'all, from God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
1.4: I always thank God for y'all, 'cause of the grace He gave y'all through Christ Jesus.
1.5: Y'all been blessed in every way by Him—whether it's how you speak or what you know.
1.6: That gospel about Jesus? It's been proven real in y'all.
1.7: So y'all don't come up short in any spiritual gift, and you still waitin' for Jesus to be revealed.
1.8: He gon' hold y'all down 'til the end, so when He show up, y'all gon' be blameless.
1.9: And best believe—God is faithful. He the one who called y'all to be tight with His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
1.10: Now look—I'm beggin' y'all, fam, in Jesus' name: speak with one voice. Stop all this division. Y'all need to be on the same page, same mindset.
1.11: 'Cause word got back to me from Chloe's people—y'all been beefin'.
1.12: Folks out here sayin', "I rock with Paul," or "I'm team Apollos," or "Cephas my guy," or "I'm with Christ."
1.13: Is Christ split up like that? Did Paul die for you? Y'all got baptized in my name or somethin'?
1.14: I'm thankin' God I ain't baptize none of y'all except Crispus and Gaius.
1.15: That way, ain't nobody out here sayin' I baptized folks in my name.
1.16: Oh—and Stephanas' household too, I did them. Can't remember if I baptized anybody else.
1.17: But real talk, Christ ain't send me to baptize—He sent me to preach the gospel. And not with big words or fancy talk, so the cross of Christ don't lose its power.
1.18: Folks who reject God think the cross is foolish. But for us who believe and gettin' saved? That's God's power right there.
1.19: Scripture say: "I'll shut down the wisdom of the wise, And cancel out the understanding of the smart folks."
1.20: So where the wise ones at? The scholars? The deep debaters of the day? Ain't God flipped this world's wisdom upside down?
1.21: See, the world thought it could find God through its own wisdom—but that ain't how God played it. He decided to use what the world calls "foolishness"—this gospel message—to save those who believe.
1.22: Jews want signs. Greeks want wisdom.
1.23: But we out here preachin' Christ crucified. To Jews, that's a stumbling block. To Gentiles, that's nonsense.
1.24: But to the ones who been called—Jew or Gentile—Christ is God's power and God's wisdom.
1.25: Even God's "foolishness" outsmarts man's brilliance. And His "weakness" stronger than anything man can throw.
1.26: Think about who y'all are, fam. Not many of y'all were considered wise by the world's standards. Not a lot of power or clout.
1.27: But God chose the so-called "foolish" to shame the wise. He chose the weak to humble the strong.
1.28: He chose the low-down, overlooked, and written-off things—to take down the ones that think they up.
1.29: So nobody can flex in God's presence like they did it on their own.
1.30: But it's because of God that you in Christ Jesus. And Christ became everything we needed—God's wisdom, our righteousness, our sanctification, and our redemption.
1.31: So like the Word say, "If you gon' brag, brag on the Lord."

2.1: When I pulled up to y'all, fam, I wasn't tryin' to impress with fancy talk or deep philosophy when I shared God's message.
2.2: I made up my mind to keep it simple—just Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.
2.3: I came in weak, nervous, and shook up.
2.4: My message and preachin'? It wasn't slick talk or human wisdom—it was straight-up Spirit and power.
2.5: That way, your faith wouldn't be built on somebody's intellect, but on the power of God.
2.6: Now don't get it twisted—we do speak wisdom, but only to the ones who are spiritually mature. And it ain't the kind of wisdom this world respects, or the kind these so-called "powerful" folks got—they all on their way out.
2.7: We speak a secret wisdom from God, hidden from the jump—something God set in motion before time to bring us glory.
2.8: None of the rulers of this world had a clue—if they did, they never would've crucified the Lord of Glory.
2.9: Like Scripture say: "Eye ain't seen, ear ain't heard, It ain't even entered the mind of man What God got in store for the ones who love Him."
2.10: But God let us in on it—through the Spirit. The Spirit dig deep, searchin' everything—even the secret stuff of God.
2.11: Who knows what's really goin' on inside a person except that person's own spirit? Same way, nobody knows what's goin' on with God—except God's Spirit.
2.12: But we didn't receive the world's spirit—we got the Spirit that's from God. So now we can understand what God already gave us, for free.
2.13: And when we speak on these things, we don't use human-taught words. We speak with what the Holy Spirit teaches—spiritual language for spiritual truths.
2.14: See, the natural mind can't get with the things of God's Spirit. It sound like nonsense. You can't understand spiritual things without spiritual vision.
2.15: But the one who's spiritual can recognize what's real—and no one else got the right to size them up.
2.16: Who can tell the Lord what to do? Who can give Him advice? But we got the mind of Christ.

3.1: Look, fam—when I first came to y'all, I couldn't even talk to you like spiritual folks. I had to speak to y'all like y'all still in the flesh—like spiritual babies in Christ.
3.2: I had to feed you milk, not solid food. Y'all wasn't ready then, and to be honest… y'all still ain't ready now.
3.3: 'Cause y'all still actin' carnal. You got envy, drama, and division all up in the church. Ain't that proof you still movin' like the world?
3.4: When one person say, "I'm team Paul," and another, "I ride with Apollos," y'all just bein' human. That ain't Spirit-led behavior.
3.5: Who am I? Who Apollos? We just servants God used so y'all could believe. Each of us just did what the Lord gave us to do.
3.6: I planted the seed. Apollos came through and watered it. But God is the one who made it grow.
3.7: So the one who plants and the one who waters? We ain't nothin' without God who brings the increase.
3.8: The planter and the waterer got the same goal, and each one gon' get paid based on their grind.
3.9: We all workin' with God. Y'all are God's field. Y'all are God's building.
3.10: By God's grace, I laid the foundation like a wise master builder. Now others building on it. But everybody need to check how they building.
3.11: Ain't no other foundation but Jesus Christ. That's the only one that counts.
3.12: Now if you build on that foundation with gold, silver, jewels—or wood, hay, and straw—
3.13: What you build gon' get tested. Fire gon' reveal it on that Day. Fire gon' show if your work was real.
3.14: If your work stands the fire, you get your reward.
3.15: If it burns up? You gon' take a loss—but you still saved… just barely, like somebody runnin' out a house on fire.
3.16: Don't you know you the temple of God, and His Spirit live in you?
3.17: If somebody out here tryna wreck God's temple, God gon' wreck them. The temple is holy—and that temple is you.
3.18: Stop foolin' yourself. If you think you wise by the world's standards, you need to become a fool for real so you can become truly wise.
3.19: The world's wisdom? God calls it foolishness. Scripture says: "He catches the wise slippin' with their own schemes."
3.20: And again: "The Lord knows how empty and pointless the so-called 'wise' really think."
3.21: So stop braggin' on human leaders. Don't worship folks. Everything already belong to y'all anyway—
3.22: Whether it's Paul, Apollos, Cephas, the world, life, death, what's now, or what's comin'—all of it is yours.
3.23: And you belong to Christ. And Christ belongs to God.

4.1: So here's how y'all should think of us—we servants of Christ, holdin' it down as stewards of God's mysteries.
4.2: And what's required of a steward? That they be faithful. Period.
4.3: Truth be told, I don't lose sleep over y'all judging me—or any human court for that matter. I don't even judge myself like that.
4.4: I ain't got nothin' on my record that I know of—but that don't make me right. The Lord's the One who judges me.
4.5: So don't go judging before it's time. Wait 'til the Lord shows up. He gon' bring everything in the dark into the light and expose what's really in people's hearts. That's when folks'll get praise—from God.
4.6: Fam, I been usin' me and Apollos as examples to teach y'all somethin'—don't go beyond what's written. Stay grounded, so you don't get puffed up sayin' "I'm with him" or "I roll with them."
4.7: What makes you so different anyway? What do you have that you didn't receive? And if you did receive it, why you actin' like you got it all on your own?
4.8: Oh, y'all think y'all full now? Rich already? Reignin' like royalty? I wish y'all really was—then maybe we could reign with you.
4.9: But from where I'm sittin', God got us apostles lookin' like we last in line—like folks already sentenced to death. We on display out here—spectacles to the world, angels, and people alike.
4.10: We out here lookin' like fools for Christ… while y'all lookin' wise. We weak… y'all strong. Y'all respected… we dishonored.
4.11: Right now, we hungry and thirsty, wearin' rags, takin' beatings, and sleepin' outside.
4.12: We workin' with our own hands. When folks cuss us out, we bless 'em. When they come for us, we take it.
4.13: When they slander us, we still speak peace. We the bottom of the barrel—the world's trash, tossed aside to this day.
4.14: I ain't sayin' all this to shame you—I'm talkin' to you like you my own kids. I'm warnin' you.
4.15: You might have a bunch of church teachers, but you don't have many spiritual fathers. In Christ, I became your father through the gospel.
4.16: So I'm tellin' you—follow my example.
4.17: That's why I'm sendin' Timothy, my beloved and faithful son in the Lord. He gon' remind y'all how I move in Christ—same way I teach everywhere, in every church.
4.18: Some of y'all gettin' cocky like I ain't really comin'.
4.19: But I am comin'—if the Lord say the same. And when I do, I ain't gon' just listen to y'all talk—I'm lookin' for power.
4.20: 'Cause the Kingdom of God ain't just words. It's power.
4.21: So what's the vibe? You want me to come with a rod—or come in love, with a gentle spirit?

5.1: Yo, it's wild out here—I'm hearin' that there's sexual sin goin' down among y'all that even folks in the streets don't do. Somebody sleepin' with his father's wife?!
5.2: And instead of mournin' and checkin' that, y'all puffed up—like it's whatever. Nah. That man shoulda been put out the community.
5.3: I might not be there in person, but in spirit? I already passed judgment like I'm sittin' right there.
5.4: So when y'all come together in Jesus' name, with my spirit present and His power movin'—
5.5: Hand that man over to Satan, so his flesh can get broken down, but his spirit might still get saved when Jesus returns.
5.6: Y'all out here boastin'? That ain't good. Don't you know a little yeast spreads through the whole batch of dough?
5.7: So clean out that old yeast—that sin—so y'all can be a new batch. You already been made new.
5.8: Let's live this thing for real—not with old, moldy ways like malice and wickedness, but with real-deal sincerity and truth.
5.9: I told y'all before—don't mix with folks who livin' in sexual sin.
5.10: And I wasn't talkin' 'bout folks outside the church—that'd mean leavin' the whole world.
5.11: I'm talkin' 'bout folks who say they're brothers and sisters in Christ but still livin' foul—whether they're sexually immoral, greedy, worshippin' idols, talkin' reckless, drunk all the time, or out here robbin' folks. Don't even eat with people like that.
5.12: I ain't worried about judgin' outsiders—that's God's job.
5.13: But folks on the inside? We supposed to hold each other accountable. Like Scripture says: "Put that evil person out from among you."

6.1: For real, y'all? You got beef with a brother or sister and you takin' it to court—in front of unbelievers—instead of bringin' it to the church?
6.2: Don't you know the saints gon' judge the world? And if that's true, can't y'all handle these small disputes?
6.3: Don't you know we gon' judge angels? So why can't y'all settle things in this life?
6.4: If you got issues to judge, why let folks the church don't even respect handle it?
6.5: I'm sayin' this to shame you a little—like, really? Ain't there one wise person among y'all who can mediate between brothers and sisters?
6.6: Instead, y'all takin' each other to court, and lettin' unbelievers watch us tear each other apart. That's not it.
6.7: Honestly, the fact that y'all even suin' each other shows it's already a loss. Why not just take the hit? Why not just let yourself get played?
6.8: But nah, y'all doin' the dirt yourselves—and doin' it to your own family in Christ.
6.9: Don't you know that folks livin' in unrighteousness ain't inheriting the Kingdom? Don't get it twisted.
6.10: folks stealing, greedy, gettin' drunk, talkin' reckless, or extorting folks—none of them gettin' in if they stay in it.
6.11: And let's keep it real—some of y'all used to be like that. But now you been washed. You been made holy. You been justified in Jesus' name and by the Spirit of our God.
6.12: "Everything's allowed for me"—okay, cool, but that don't mean everything good for you. And just 'cause it's allowed don't mean I'ma let it control me.
6.13: Yeah, food for the stomach and stomach for food—but God gon' do away with both. But your body? It ain't for sexual sin—it's for the Lord. And He for your body.
6.14: Just like God raised Jesus, He gon' raise us too—with that same power.
6.15: Don't you know your body is part of Christ now? So how you gon' link Christ to a prostitute? No way.
6.16: When you sleep with somebody, y'all become one flesh. That's not just physical—it's spiritual.
6.17: But when you're joined to the Lord? You one spirit with Him.
6.18: Run from sexual sin. Fast. That one hit different. Other sins happen outside your body—but this one? You hurtin' yourself.
6.19: Don't you know your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit? He's in you. God gave Him to you. You don't even belong to yourself.
6.20: You were bought with a price. So use your body—and your whole being—to glorify God. That's what it's for.

7.1: So, about what y'all wrote me—yeah, it's good for a man to stay single and not be all touchy with a woman.
7.2: But since sexual temptation out here heavy, every man should have his own wife, and every woman her own husband.
7.3: Husbands, show your wife the love and affection she's due—and wives, same goes for y'all.
7.4: Your body ain't just yours anymore. Wives, your husband got claim too. And husbands? Your wife got claim on you, period.
7.5: Don't hold out on each other—unless y'all agree for a season so y'all can fast and pray. But come back together, or the enemy gon' use that against y'all.
7.6: I'm sayin' that as a suggestion, not a hard rule.
7.7: I wish everybody could stay single like me—but hey, everybody got their own gift from God.
7.8: To the single folks and widows: I think it's best if you stay single like I am.
7.9: But if you can't control yourself, it's better to get married than to burn with passion and frustration.
7.10: To the married, this ain't just me talkin'—this from the Lord: a wife shouldn't leave her husband.
7.11: But if she does, she should stay single or get back with her man. And husbands? Don't divorce your wife.
7.12: Now for the rest of y'all—this is me, not the Lord directly: if a man got a wife who ain't a believer, but she's down to stay, don't leave her.
7.13: And if a woman got a man who ain't saved, but he wanna stay with her, let him.
7.14: That believing spouse brings spiritual cover—the unbelieving spouse is touched by that, and the kids are covered too.
7.15: But if the unbeliever wants out, let 'em go. Ain't no chains in situations like that. God called us to peace, not chaos.
7.16: You don't know, sis, if you might lead your man to salvation. And bro, you don't know if you might save your wife.
7.17: However God had you livin' when He called you? Walk in that. That's the same rule I give in every church.
7.18: You were circumcised when you got called? Don't undo it. Uncircumcised? Don't get cut now.
7.19: That outward stuff don't matter. What matters is keepin' God's commandments.
7.20: So however you were when God called you? Stay there.
7.21: You were a slave when you got saved? Don't stress. But if you get a chance to be free, take it.
7.22: 'Cause if you a slave and get saved, you still free in the Lord. And if you free, you still got a master—Christ.
7.23: God paid for you with blood. Don't let people make you slaves again.
7.24: Fam, wherever you were when God called you—stay close to Him right there.
7.25: Now about virgins—I don't have a direct command from the Lord, but I'm givin' my take, since God trusted me with this.
7.26: Because of the hard times right now, I think it's good to stay as you are.
7.27: Got a wife? Don't try to dip. Don't got a wife? Don't go lookin' hard either.
7.28: But if you do get married, you ain't sinnin'. And if a virgin marries, she ain't sinnin' either. Just know—it ain't all roses. Marriage comes with struggle, and I'm tryna spare y'all some of that.
7.29: Look, fam—the time is short. From now on, folks with spouses should live like that ain't their whole identity.
7.30: Mourners—don't get stuck there. Rejoicers—don't get lost in it. Shoppers—don't get attached to the stuff.
7.31: Use the world, but don't abuse it. This world as we know it? It's passin' away.
7.32: I want y'all to live stress-free. Unmarried folks can stay locked in on the Lord—how to please Him.
7.33: But married folks gotta split attention—they tryna please their spouse too.
7.34: Same with women: the single ones focus on the Lord, tryna live holy in body and spirit. Married ones focus on their husband.
7.35: I'm sayin' this to help you—not to trap you. I want you to be able to serve the Lord without distractions.
7.36: If a man think he's actin' wrong toward his girl, and she's grown and ready, and they both know it's time—go ahead and marry. That's not a sin.
7.37: But if he's settled in his heart, got self-control, and decides not to marry her, that's cool too.
7.38: Bottom line: both options are good. But the one who holds off on marriage? He doin' better.
7.39: A wife is bound to her man as long as he's alive. But if he dies, she's free to marry whoever—as long as he's in the Lord.
7.40: But in my opinion, she'd be happier stayin' single—and I think I'm speakin' with the Spirit of God on that.

8.1: Now let's talk about food that's been offered to idols. Yeah, we all got knowledge—but listen: knowledge can puff your head up, but love? Love builds people up.
8.2: If you think you know everything, you probably don't even know what you need to know yet.
8.3: But if you love God? God knows you. That's what really matters.
8.4: So about eatin' food that was offered to idols—we know idols ain't nothin'. Ain't no real gods behind them statues.
8.5: Even though folks out here talkin' about "gods" in the sky and lords on the earth,
8.6: for us, there's only one God—the Father, who everything came from and who we live for. And one Lord—Jesus Christ—who made everything possible and keeps us movin'.
8.7: But not everybody got that kind of understanding. Some folks still see that meat as tied to idol worship, and when they eat it, their conscience gets messed up—'cause it feels wrong to them.
8.8: Truth is, God don't care about what's on your plate. You don't get extra credit for eatin', and you ain't fallin' off for not eatin'.
8.9: But be careful that your freedom don't turn into a trap for somebody else who's weaker in the faith.
8.10: Like, if somebody sees you eatin' at an idol's temple and they not mature in their faith, they might think it's okay and copy you—even though it still feels wrong to them.
8.11: And now, because of your "knowledge," your weaker brother or sister—who Christ died for—might fall off.
8.12: When you hurt their conscience like that, you ain't just sinnin' against them—you sinnin' against Christ.
8.13: So Paul says, "If what I'm eatin' is gon' make my brother fall off, I'll never eat meat again." He'd rather give it up than let it be a stumbling block.

9.1: Ain't I an apostle? Ain't I free? Didn't I see Jesus with my own eyes? Ain't y'all my work in the Lord?
9.2: Even if other folks don't see me as an apostle, y'all know what it is. You the proof of my assignment.
9.3: So here's my defense to the folks questioning me—
9.4: Don't I got the right to eat and drink like everybody else?
9.5: Don't I got the right to travel with a believing wife, like the other apostles do? Like Jesus' brothers? Like Peter (Cephas)?
9.6: Or is it just me and Barnabas who gotta grind without support?
9.7: Who goes to war payin' their own way? Who plants a vineyard and don't eat off it? Who takes care of sheep but don't drink the milk?
9.8: I ain't just talkin' from a human angle—the law backs me up too.
9.9: Moses said, "Don't muzzle the ox while it's treading grain." You think God was talkin' about oxen only?
9.10: Nah, He said that for our sake. Folks who do the work supposed to benefit from the work.
9.11: So if we planted spiritual seed in y'all, is it too much to receive a little material help back?
9.12: If others can do that with you, shouldn't we even more? But we ain't exercise that right—we takin' the high road, so nothin' gets in the way of the gospel.
9.13: Don't y'all know that temple workers ate from what was brought to the temple? Same thing with altar workers—they got a portion too.
9.14: In the same way, Jesus said those who preach the gospel should live from the gospel.
9.15: But me? I didn't use any of that. And I ain't sayin' this so y'all start cuttin' checks. I'd rather die than have somebody act like I'm in this for the money.
9.16: Preachin' the gospel ain't a flex—it's a calling. I have to do this. I'd be lost if I didn't.
9.17: If I do it willingly, there's reward. If not, it's still my assignment.
9.18: So what's my reward? That I preach the gospel for free, without strings, without manipulation. No abuse of authority here.
9.19: Even though I'm free, I made myself a servant to everybody—just to win more souls.
9.20: To the Jews? I move like a Jew to win them. To folks under the law? I meet them where they are.
9.21: To those outside the law? I relate too—but I'm still under Christ's law, always.
9.22: To the weak? I became weak. I've become all things to all people so I might save some.
9.23: And I do it all for the gospel—so I can share in its blessings with y'all.
9.24: Y'all know how in a race, everybody runs—but only one wins? Run like you tryin' to win.
9.25: Athletes train hard for a crown that fades. But we chasin' a crown that's eternal.
9.26: I don't run with no confusion. I don't fight like I'm swingin' at air.
9.27: I keep my body in check—I make it my servant. 'Cause I refuse to preach to others and end up disqualified myself.

10.1: Look fam, I don't want y'all out here clueless. Our ancestors all had the same experience—they were covered by the cloud, walked through the sea,
10.2: and were basically baptized into Moses when they went through that water.
10.3: They all ate the same spiritual food,
10.4: drank the same spiritual drink—from the spiritual Rock that followed them. And that Rock? That was Christ.
10.5: But even after all that, most of them didn't please God—they died out there in the wilderness.
10.6: That right there? That's a warning for us—not to chase evil desires like they did.
10.7: Don't worship idols like some of them did. Remember what's written: "The people sat down to eat and drink, then got up to wild out."
10.8: Don't get caught in sexual sin either. They did, and 23,000 of them dropped in one day.
10.9: Don't test Christ like they did, or you'll end up like them—gettin' destroyed by snakes.
10.10: And don't be out here complainin' and grumblin'. Some of them did that too and got handled by the destroyer.
10.11: All of that happened as a warning for us. It's written down so we stay sharp—especially since we livin' in these last days.
10.12: So if you think you stand strong—watch your step, or you might fall.
10.13: Any temptation you facin'? It ain't new. Everybody go through it. But God is faithful—He won't let you face more than you can handle. And when it does come, He always provides a way out so you can make it through.
10.14: So beloved, run from idolatry. Don't play with it.
10.15: I'm talkin' to folks with sense—judge for yourself what I'm sayin'.
10.16: When we bless the cup, we're sharin' in the blood of Christ. When we break the bread, we're sharin' in His body.
10.17: We might be many, but we one body 'cause we all eat from the same bread—Christ.
10.18: Look at Israel—when they ate from the altar, they were participating in the sacrifice, right?
10.19: I'm not sayin' idols are real or the food itself is somethin'—
10.20: But what folks sacrifice to idols, they really sacrificin' to demons. And I ain't tryna see y'all mixin' with that.
10.21: You can't drink from the Lord's cup and from the demons' cup. You can't sit at both tables.
10.22: You tryna make God jealous? You think you stronger than Him?
10.23: Sure, "everything's lawful"—but that don't mean it's helpful. Just 'cause you can do it don't mean it builds anybody up.
10.24: Don't just look out for yourself—look out for others too.
10.25: If you buy meat from the market, eat it—don't ask no questions for your conscience's sake.
10.26: Remember: "The earth is the Lord's and everything in it."
10.27: If somebody who don't believe invites you to dinner and you down to go, eat what's served. No need to interrogate the menu.
10.28: But if they say, "This meat was offered to idols," then don't eat it—not for your sake, but for theirs.
10.29: I'm talkin' about their conscience, not yours. Why should my freedom be judged by someone else's convictions?
10.30: If I give thanks over it, why I gotta be criticized for it?
10.31: Whether you eat, drink, or whatever you do—do it all for God's glory.
10.32: Don't trip folks up—whether they're Jewish, Gentile, or part of the church.
10.33: I try to meet folks where they are, not just for my gain, but so they can be saved.

11.1: Y'all should follow my example—'cause I'm followin' Christ.
11.2: I respect that y'all still remember what I taught and try to keep the traditions I handed down.
11.3: But let me make this clear: Christ is the head over every man, man is the head over woman, and God is the head over Christ.
11.4: If a man prays or prophesies with something coverin' his head, he disrespectin' his spiritual head.
11.5: And if a woman prays or prophesies with her head uncovered, she disrespectin' hers—it's like she out here with her head shaved off.
11.6: If she won't cover her head, she might as well cut it off. But if that's shameful, then she need to keep it covered.
11.7: A man shouldn't have his head covered, 'cause he reflects God's image and glory. But woman? She's the glory of man.
11.8: Man ain't come from woman—woman came from man.
11.9: And man wasn't made for woman's sake, but woman for man's.
11.10: That's why a woman should wear a symbol of authority on her head—outta respect for the angels, too.
11.11: But hold up—it ain't about who's better. In the Lord, man and woman need each other.
11.12: Yeah, woman came from man, but now every man since been born through a woman—and God is the source of it all.
11.13: Y'all judge it for yourselves—is it really proper for a woman to be praying with her head uncovered?
11.14: Nature itself teach you—if a man got long hair, it's seen as dishonor.
11.15: But a woman with long hair? That's her glory. God gave her hair as a natural covering.
11.16: If somebody wanna argue? Ain't nobody in the churches of God out here makin' this a whole thing—we don't have that kind of drama.
11.17: Now about this next thing—I can't praise y'all. 'Cause when y'all come together, it ain't helpin' y'all—it's hurtin'.
11.18: I'm hearin' there's division in the church when y'all gather. And honestly? I believe some of it.
11.19: Maybe it gotta be that way so the real ones can stand out.
11.20: But when y'all come together to eat, it ain't really the Lord's Supper.
11.21: Folks out here eatin' early, takin' they own food—one person hungry, another drunk!
11.22: Don't y'all got houses for that? Or do you just not care about the church or shame folks who ain't got much? I ain't praisin' that. That's a mess.
11.23: Let me remind y'all what the Lord gave me: The same night Jesus was betrayed, He took bread,
11.24: gave thanks, broke it and said, "This is My body, broken for y'all. Eat this to remember Me."
11.25: Then He took the cup and said, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Drink it to remember Me."
11.26: So every time y'all eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death—until He comes back.
11.27: So if you eat or drink from the Lord's table in a reckless or unworthy way, you guilty of disrespectin' His body and blood.
11.28: Check yourself. Do a self-check before you eat that bread and sip that cup.
11.29: 'Cause if you don't discern the Lord's body right, you bringin' judgment on yourself.
11.30: That's why some of y'all are weak, sick—and some even sleepin' in the grave.
11.31: If we judged ourselves first, we wouldn't have to be judged.
11.32: But when God does judge us, it's to correct us—not to destroy us like the world.
11.33: So fam, when y'all come together to eat—wait on each other.
11.34: If you starving, eat at home. Don't turn communion into a judgment zone. I'll deal with the rest when I come in person.

12.1: Now let's talk spiritual gifts, fam—I don't want y'all to be clueless out here.
12.2: Remember, back in the day y'all used to follow after dumb idols that couldn't speak—y'all didn't know no better.
12.3: So let me clear this up: nobody talkin' by the Spirit of God is gon' curse Jesus. And ain't nobody sayin' "Jesus is Lord" for real unless the Holy Spirit gave 'em that revelation.
12.4: We got different kinds of gifts, but it's the same Spirit that hands them out.
12.5: Different ways to serve, but it's the same Lord.
12.6: Different ways God moves, but it's still the same God workin' through everybody.
12.7: The Holy Spirit shows up through each one of us—for the benefit of the whole squad.
12.8: Some get wisdom through the Spirit. Some get knowledge.
12.9: Others get deep faith. Some got the gift to heal folks.
12.10: Some can do miracles, some can prophesy. Others can tell the difference between what's from God and what's not. Some speak in all kinds of tongues, and others can interpret those tongues.
12.11: But it's one Spirit doing all this—He hands out the gifts however He wants, to whoever He chooses.
12.12: Just like the body got many parts but still one body, same thing with Christ's people.
12.13: We all got baptized into one body—don't matter if you Jew, Greek, slave, or free—we all drinkin' from the same Spirit.
12.14: The body ain't made of just one part—it's many.
12.15: The foot can't say, "I ain't a hand so I don't belong." Nah—you still part of the body.
12.16: Same if the ear say, "I ain't an eye, so I don't count." You still matter.
12.17: If the whole body was one big eye, who'd hear? If we all hearing, who gon' smell?
12.18: God placed every part exactly where He wanted it in the body.
12.19: If everything was just one part, that wouldn't even be a body.
12.20: But we got many parts—still one body.
12.21: The eye can't say to the hand, "I don't need you." The head can't tell the feet, "Y'all irrelevant."
12.22: Nah—those parts that seem weaker? They essential.
12.23: The ones we don't give much credit to? God puts extra honor on them.
12.24: Some parts need no help—but God arranged the body so every part gets its respect.
12.25: That way, there's no division. Every part lookin' out for the others.
12.26: If one part hurt, the whole body feel it. If one part gets lifted up, the whole body should celebrate.
12.27: Y'all are Christ's body—and every one of y'all got a part to play.
12.28: God placed different roles in the church: First—apostles, Second—prophets, Third—teachers, Then miracle workers, healing hands, helpers, organizers, and those speakin' in different tongues.
12.29: Is everybody an apostle? Everybody a prophet? Everybody a teacher? Can everybody do miracles?
12.30: Can everybody heal, speak in tongues, or interpret them?
12.31: Nah—but you should want the best gifts God got for you. But I'ma show y'all an even better way…

13.1: I could speak every language on earth—even heavenly ones—but if I ain't got love, I'm just makin' noise. Just loud cymbals with no soul.
13.2: I could prophesy like a prophet, understand every deep mystery, hold all the knowledge, and have enough faith to move whole mountains—but if love ain't in me, I'm nothin'.
13.3: I could give away everything I got to feed the poor. I could even give up my body for the cause. But if I ain't got love? It don't mean nothin'.
13.4: Love is patient. Love is kind. It don't envy, it don't show off, it don't walk around with a big head.
13.5: Love don't act rude. It don't make it all about self. It don't get triggered easy and don't keep receipts of wrongs.
13.6: Love don't celebrate mess—it celebrates truth.
13.7: Love holds it down, believes the best, stays hopeful, and don't give up.
13.8: Love never fails—never. Prophecies? They gon' expire. Speaking in tongues? That season gon' pass. Even knowledge? One day, it'll fade.
13.9: 'Cause right now, we only know a little, and we only speak a little of what's true.
13.10: But when perfection comes? That partial stuff gets retired.
13.11: When I was a child, I talked, thought, and reasoned like a child. But when I grew up, I left all that childish stuff behind.
13.12: Right now, it's like lookin' at life through a foggy mirror. But later? We gon' see it clear. Face to face. Right now, I only know part of the picture. But one day, I'ma know fully—just like God fully knows me now.
13.13: So these three still stand strong: faith, hope, and love. But the greatest one? Love.

14.1: Run after love first. But also go after spiritual gifts—especially prophecy.
14.2: See, when you speak in tongues, you talkin' to God, not people. Nobody understands you, 'cause you speakin' mysteries in the Spirit.
14.3: But if you prophesy, you speak life—building folks up, encouraging them, and bringin' comfort.
14.4: Tongues might build you up, but prophecy builds the whole church.
14.5: I'd love for all y'all to speak in tongues, but even more for y'all to prophesy. Prophecy does more unless someone interprets the tongue so the church can grow from it.
14.6: So what good is it if I come speakin' in tongues but don't bring a revelation, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching?
14.7: Think about instruments—flutes or harps. If they just play random sounds, who knows the melody?
14.8: If a trumpet makes a wild, unclear sound, who gon' know it's time for battle?
14.9: Same with y'all—if your words ain't clear, folks just hearin' noise. Ain't nobody gettin' helped.
14.10: There's all kinds of languages in the world, and they all matter.
14.11: But if I don't understand your language, I'm a foreigner to you—and you to me.
14.12: So since y'all so hype about spiritual gifts, focus on helping the whole church, not just flexin'.
14.13: If you speak in tongues, pray for the power to interpret it.
14.14: 'Cause when I pray in tongues, it's my spirit prayin'—but my mind ain't catching none of it.
14.15: So what do I do? I pray in the Spirit and with understanding. I sing in the Spirit and with understanding.
14.16: Otherwise, how can someone say "Amen" if they don't know what you sayin'?
14.17: You might be giving thanks, but the other person ain't bein' built up.
14.18: I thank God I speak in tongues more than all y'all.
14.19: But in church? I'd rather speak 5 words with understanding to teach folks than 10,000 words nobody understands.
14.20: Stop actin' childish with understanding. Be innocent when it comes to evil—but grown in how you think.
14.21: Scripture says, "I'll speak to this people through other tongues… and still, they won't listen."
14.22: So tongues are a sign for unbelievers, not for believers. Prophecy, though? That's for the believers.
14.23: If the whole church speakin' in tongues and somebody new walks in, they'll think y'all lost it.
14.24: But if everybody prophesies, that person gon' get convicted and called out by the Spirit.
14.25: Their whole heart gon' be laid bare, and they'll fall down and say, "God is really here."
14.26: So what's the move, fam? When y'all gather, everybody brings somethin'—a song, a word, a tongue, a revelation, an interpretation. Let it all be done to build folks up.
14.27: If you speak in tongues, let two or three speak—one at a time—and make sure someone interprets.
14.28: No interpreter? Then keep it to yourself and God.
14.29: Let two or three prophets speak, and others should weigh what's said.
14.30: If someone else gets a word mid-service, the first speaker should chill.
14.31: You can all take turns prophesyin' so everyone can learn and be encouraged.
14.32: And prophets? Your spirit stays in check. You ain't outta control.
14.33: 'Cause God ain't about confusion—He's about peace, just like in all His churches.
14.34: Let the women be silent in church. They not permitted to speak but should stay in order, like the law says.
14.35: If they got questions, they can ask their husbands at home—it ain't a good look for women to speak up during church time.
14.36: Y'all think the Word of God started with you? Or only came to you?
14.37: If you really a prophet or spiritually mature, you'll know what I'm saying is from the Lord.
14.38: But if somebody wanna act brand new and ignore it—let 'em stay ignorant.
14.39: So fam—go after prophecy, and don't block folks from speakin' in tongues.
14.40: But make sure everything is done decently, and in order.

15.1: Let me remind y'all of the gospel I already preached to you—the one y'all received and stand on.
15.2: That message? It's what saves you if you hold on tight—unless your belief was empty from the jump.
15.3: Here's what I handed y'all first: Christ died for our sins, just like Scripture said.
15.4: He was buried. Then on the third day? He got up—just like Scripture said.
15.5: He showed Himself to Peter, then to the twelve.
15.6: After that, over 500 folks saw Him at once—most of 'em still around, but some have passed on.
15.7: Then James saw Him. Then the rest of the apostles.
15.8: And last of all, He appeared to me—like one born late to the party.
15.9: I'm the least of the apostles—not even worthy to be called that, 'cause I used to go hard against God's church.
15.10: But by God's grace? I am what I am. And that grace wasn't wasted—I worked harder than all of them. But really? It was God's grace workin' through me.
15.11: Whether it was me or them preachin'—we all gave the same gospel, and y'all believed it.
15.12: So if we preach that Christ rose from the dead, how y'all gon' say there ain't no resurrection?
15.13: If the dead don't rise, then Christ ain't risen.
15.14: And if Christ ain't risen, our whole message is empty—and so is your faith.
15.15: We'd be out here lyin' on God, sayin' He raised Christ—if He really didn't.
15.16: If the dead don't rise, then Jesus ain't rise.
15.17: And if Jesus ain't rise, your faith is useless and you still stuck in your sins.
15.18: That means everybody who died in Christ is just… gone.
15.19: If this life is the only hope we got in Christ? We the most pitiful folks out here.
15.20: But the truth is—Christ has been raised! He the first one out the grave, but not the last.
15.21: Death came through one man—Adam. So resurrection comes through another man—Jesus.
15.22: In Adam, everybody dies. But in Christ, everybody gets brought back to life.
15.23: Christ rose first. Then, when He comes back, His people will rise too.
15.24: Then comes the end—Jesus hands the kingdom back to the Father, after He shuts down every ruler and all power.
15.25: He gon' reign till every enemy is under His feet.
15.26: The last enemy to get destroyed? Death.
15.27: God put everything under His feet. But obviously, God the Father ain't included in that "everything."
15.28: When it's all said and done, the Son Himself will submit to the Father, so God can be all in all.
15.29: If there's no resurrection, why would folks even get baptized for the dead? What's that doin'?
15.30: And why would we risk our lives daily?
15.31: I die daily for this gospel. That's facts.
15.32: If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for no resurrection? That was pointless. Might as well just say, "Let's eat and drink, 'cause tomorrow we dead."
15.33: Don't get played: "Bad company corrupts good character."
15.34: Wake up. Start livin' right. Some of y'all don't even know God—and that's shameful.
15.35: Somebody might ask, "How the dead gon' be raised? What kind of body they comin' back with?"
15.36: That's a silly question. When you plant a seed, it don't come alive unless it dies first.
15.37: You don't plant the full-grown tree—you plant the seed.
15.38: And God gives it the body He wants. Every seed has its own body.
15.39: All flesh ain't the same—human flesh ain't the same as animals, fish, or birds.
15.40: There's heavenly bodies and earthly bodies—and each one got its own kind of glory.
15.41: The sun got one kind. The moon got another. Stars got theirs—and even stars don't shine the same.
15.42: Same way with the resurrection: Buried in corruption—raised in perfection.
15.43: Buried in dishonor—raised in glory. Buried in weakness—raised in power.
15.44: Buried a natural body—raised a spiritual one. There's a natural body and a spiritual one.
15.45: Adam, the first man, became a living being. But Jesus, the last Adam, became a life-giving Spirit.
15.46: The natural came first, then the spiritual.
15.47: First man was made of dust. Second man came from heaven.
15.48: Earth people like the dusty man. Heaven people like the heavenly one.
15.49: And just like we wore the image of the dusty one, we gon' wear the image of the heavenly one too.
15.50: Listen fam—flesh and blood can't inherit God's kingdom. Corruption can't walk into eternity.
15.51: But here's the mystery: We not all gon' die—but we all gon' be changed.
15.52: In a flash, in the blink of an eye, when the last trumpet sounds—the dead will rise incorruptible, and we'll be changed too.
15.53: This corrupt body gotta be clothed with the incorruptible. This mortal gotta put on immortality.
15.54: And when that happens? The prophecy comes true: "Death is swallowed up in victory."
15.55: "Death, where your sting at? Grave, where your W at?"
15.56: The sting of death is sin, and sin gets its strength from the law.
15.57: But thanks be to God, who gives us the win through our Lord Jesus Christ!
15.58: So fam, stay locked in. Don't move. Keep doin' God's work like it matters—'cause it ain't in vain. God sees you.

16.1: Now about the money for the church fam in need—I gave this instruction to the churches in Galatia, and I need y'all to do the same.
16.2: On the first day of the week, everybody should set aside a little somethin', based on how blessed they been. That way, we don't gotta do a last-minute collection when I get there.
16.3: When I come through, whoever y'all trust and choose, I'll send them with the gift to Jerusalem.
16.4: And if it make sense for me to go too, they can roll with me.
16.5: I plan to come see y'all after I go through Macedonia (I'm already on the way).
16.6: Might even chill with y'all for a bit—or stay through the winter—so y'all can help me get to the next stop.
16.7: I don't wanna just pass through real quick. I'm tryin' to spend some real time with y'all—if the Lord allows.
16.8: For now, I'm stayin' in Ephesus until Pentecost.
16.9: God opened a big door for me here—but trust, it's mad opposition too.
16.10: If Timothy pulls up, make sure he feels safe and welcomed. He's out here doin' God's work just like I am.
16.11: Don't let nobody look down on him. Show him love and send him off in peace—he's comin' back to me, and I'm waitin' on him with the crew.
16.12: About Apollos—I asked him strong to go to y'all with the brothers, but he ain't feel led to go right now. He'll come when the time's right for him.
16.13: Stay woke. Stand firm in the faith. Be bold. Be strong.
16.14: And whatever you do—do it all in love.
16.15: One more thing: y'all know Stephanas and his household were the first folks in Achaia to come to Christ, and they been servin' ever since.
16.16: So show them respect. Same for anybody workin' hard in the ministry alongside us.
16.17: I'm real glad Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus came—they filled the gap for y'all when I needed it.
16.18: They refreshed my soul—and yours too. Recognize folks like them. Real ones.
16.19: The churches out here in Asia send their love. Aquila and Priscilla say what's up in the Lord—same with the church that meets at their house.
16.20: All the brothers and sisters send love. Greet each other with a holy kiss.
16.21: I'm writin' this last part with my own hand—Paul.
16.22: If anybody out here don't love the Lord? Let 'em be cursed. Come on, Jesus—we ready.
16.23: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with y'all.
16.24: And my love? It's with every single one of y'all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
